name: No Way Out
tagline: Handle the situation no single rule can predict.
narrative: The small maze introduces a dead-end pattern that the two-rule corner brain cannot distinguish from an ordinary turn. Combine the front and right wall observations into a more specific case, then place that case above the general blocked-path rule.
objective: Navigate the 7x7 maze from start to goal, then hold on the goal for 3 ticks.
learningObjective: Combining conditions with AND (`&&`) and reasoning about ordered rules when multiple conditions could match.
intelligenceExplanation: This brain has two rules: move forward when clear, and turn right when blocked. That handles single corners, but in a maze with dead ends it will oscillate — turning right, finding a wall, turning right again, looping. Add a rule that handles the dead-end case: both ahead and right are walls. A left turn, or an about-face, breaks the cycle. Order the rules by specificity: most specific conditions at the top, most general fallbacks at the bottom. Put WHEN atGoal -> DO hold first so the robot settles at its destination.
hint: Use `wallAhead && wallRight` as the condition for a new rule that pivots left. Place it above the existing turn-right rule.
hints: Look for a situation in which the existing wallAhead rule is too general.
Combine wallAhead and wallRight with AND to describe the dead-end case.
Put WHEN wallAhead AND wallRight → pivot-left above the existing wallAhead → pivot-right rule, with the arrival rule first.
brief: Add a specific dead-end response and use it to reach the goal.
context: The starter brain handles clear corridors and ordinary corners, but not combined wall conditions.

steps.label: Describe the dead end with a combined condition
Escape the maze and settle on the goal
